sources.why: RELEASE.md names v1.1.0 as the stable contract the line is measured from, and it is the oldest revision this promise reaches back to.
A patch of the stable contract, which docs/COMPATIBILITY.md puts inside the line, so an installation that took it is an installation this release has to take too.

refused.reason: RELEASE.md excludes v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0 as an upgrade path, so the line this release upgrades from does not reach it.

docs/COMPATIBILITY.md gives a proof build no compatibility claim, and two audit files applied in it carry checksums the restored ledger does not, so its applied history cannot be upgraded by this release; the consumer pinned there moves by its own pin bump.

not a release, and its own ledger cannot be built on: it applied auth/000035 at a position the numbering later moved, so the runner refuses it as an earlier insertion ('precedes applied version 47; append a new version'); the bytes it shipped are still owed, and applied_bytes is where they are owed

fixtures.why: the volume every duration is measured against, written in the shape every supported source's own schema already holds
the second tenant, the page text, the file records and the queued events the upgrade has to carry

applied_bytes.why: the bytes first shipped as main, which an installation already holds applied; the runner compares whole files, so this release must keep these exact ones or every installed ledger rejects it
the companion file applied in the same release, held to the same rule
